theme: Buying Fruit at a Local Stall

example.thai: ช่วยปอกเปลือกให้ด้วยครับ
example.phonetic: chûuay bpɔ̀ɔk bplʉ̀ʉak hâi dûuay khráp
example.english: Please peel the skin off for me.

words.note: Fruit cart vendors will gladly peel and chop fruits like pineapple or papaya into bite-sized pieces for free.

example.thai: มะม่วงโลละกี่บาทครับ
example.phonetic: má-mûuang loo lá gìi bàat khráp
example.english: How many baht per kilo are the mangoes?

words.note: 'โล' (loo) is the ubiquitous everyday spoken short form for 'กิโลกรัม' (kilogram) across all Thai markets.

example.thai: ขอลองชิมก่อนได้ไหมครับ
example.phonetic: khɔ̌ɔ lɔɔng chim gɔ̀ɔn dâi mǎi khráp
example.english: May I taste a sample first?

words.note: Vendors selling seasonal fruits like longan, pomelo, or grapes will usually be happy to let you try a piece.

example.thai: มีลูกที่สุกพร้อมกินไหมครับ
example.phonetic: mii lûuk thîi sùk phrɔ́ɔm gin mǎi khráp
example.english: Do you have one that's ripe and ready to eat?

words.note: Say 'สุกพร้อมกิน' (sùk phrɔ́ɔm gin) if you want fruit you can enjoy immediately rather than waiting for it to ripen.

example.thai: ขอพริกเกลือเพิ่มอีกหนึ่งซองครับ
example.phonetic: khɔ̌ɔ phrík-glʉʉa phə̂əm ìik nʉ̀ng sɔɔng khráp
example.english: Can I have one more packet of chili salt, please?

words.note: This classic sweet, salty, and spicy seasoning mix is typically offered when purchasing tart fruits like guava or green mango.
